Everything needed is confirmed against the pinned source (`LMDB/lmdb` @ `700e10f9`, `libraries/liblmdb/mdb.c`).

## How readers avoid blocking the writer

**The design: MVCC + copy-on-write.** The writer never modifies a page in place, so all it needs to know from readers is *"which version of the DB they started from so we can avoid overwriting any data used in that particular version"* — that is the comment on the reader slot itself (`MDB_rxbody`, mdb.c:852–864). Readers hold **no lock for the lifetime of a read transaction**; they publish exactly one word.

**What readers record, and where.** Each reader owns one slot in the reader lock table — the `MDB_reader mti_readers[]` array inside `MDB_txninfo`, which "resides in a memory-mapped file … a different file than is used for the main database" (the lock file, mdb.c:885–887, 947–953). Each slot (`MDB_rxbody`, mdb.c:856–870, accessed via the `mr_txnid`/`mr_pid`/`mr_tid` shorthands, mdb.c:872–883) records:

- `mrb_txnid` (`mr_txnid`) — the transaction ID of the snapshot the reader started from; `(txnid_t)-1` when the slot is idle;
- `mrb_pid` (`mr_pid`) and `mrb_tid` (`mr_tid`) — owning process/thread IDs, "so that we can detect stale information" (dead processes that never cleaned up).

Slots are padded to `CACHELINE` (64) "to avoid false cache line sharing in the lock table" (mdb.c:839–844).

**The reader's only shared-memory writes are lock-free.** On read-txn start (`mdb_txn_renew0`, mdb.c:3352–3362) it copies the env's current ID without any mutex, retrying on a torn read: `do { r->mr_txnid = ti->mti_txnid; } while (r->mr_txnid != ti->mti_txnid);` ("Retry on a race, ITS#7970"). On txn end it just stores `mr_txnid = (txnid_t)-1`, also un-mutexed (mdb.c:3722–3723).

**How the writer uses this instead of blocking.** The writer scans the table with no lock in `mdb_find_oldest()` (mdb.c:2647–261), cached in `env->me_pgoldest` (mdb.c:1698; refreshed in `mdb_page_alloc`, mdb.c:2781–2823). It reclaims free pages **only from free-DB records older than the oldest live reader** (`if (oldest <= last) break;` — "Do not fetch more if the record will be too recent", mdb.c:2804–2820). Pages freed by newer transactions stay on the free list until readers advance.

**When the mutex is actually needed** — only for table bookkeeping and writer serialization, never for reading:

- `mtb_rmutex` (`mti_rmutex`, alias `env->me_rmutex`), "Mutex protecting access to this table" (mdb.c:921–923): taken **only** to claim a free slot and publish `mti_numreaders` in `mdb_txn_renew0` (mdb.c:3321–3345; `MDB_READERS_FULL` if the table is full — note the careful reset-then-publish ordering because "other code uses the reader table un-mutexed"), and by `mdb_reader_check0` to clear stale slots (mdb.c:12780+). Released immediately; never held during reads.
- `mti_wmutex` (`env->me_wmutex`): writers only — locked when the write txn begins (mdb.c:3369) and held to commit/abort ("The writer mutex was locked in mdb_txn_begin", mdb.c:3760–3762), serializing writers against each other. Readers never touch it.

So: writer-mutex held only by writers for writer serialization; reader-mutex held only for microseconds of slot allocation; the "lock" protecting a read is just the atomic `mr_txnid` word — which is also the cost: a long-lived reader pins its snapshot's pages on the free list until it ends or renews.

ANSWER: Readers take no locks for the duration of a read transaction; each writes a single word — `mr_txnid` — into its cacheline-padded slot (`MDB_reader`, fields `mrb_txnid`/`mrb_pid`/`mrb_tid`, mdb.c:856–883) in the `mti_readers[]` array of the shared `MDB_txninfo` lock file, copying `ti->mti_txnid` lock-free at txn start (ITS#7970 retry loop, mdb.c:3352) and storing `(txnid_t)-1` at end; the writer scans these IDs un-mutexed via `mdb_find_oldest()`/`me_pgoldest` and only reuses free pages older than the oldest live reader, so `mti_rmutex` is needed just for slot allocation/`mti_numreaders` updates (and stale-slot cleanup) and `mti_wmutex` is held only by writers from begin to commit — never by readers.
